name: Thalassemia

criteria.description: Presence of microcytic hypochromic anemia on complete blood count
Abnormal hemoglobin pattern detected by hemoglobin electrophoresis or HPLC
Identification of pathogenic mutations in alpha or beta globin genes by molecular genetic testing
Positive family history of thalassemia or related hemoglobinopathies
Normal or elevated serum iron and ferritin levels excluding iron deficiency anemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of microcytic anemia plus abnormal hemoglobin electrophoresis or confirmatory genetic testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of iron deficiency anemia and other hemoglobinopathies.

searchTerms: anemia with small, light-colored red cells
hemolytic anemia with young red cells
blood breakdown anemia with reticulocyte rise
enlarged liver and spleen from blood cell production outside marrow
swollen organs from blood formation in liver and spleen
jaundice due to ongoing red cell breakdown
skin and eye yellowing from hemolysis

common.symptomName: Bone deformities especially facial and cranial
Fatigue and pallor due to anemia
searchTerms: tiredness and pale skin from anemia
fatigue and pallor due to low blood counts

occasional.symptomName: Iron overload complications (cardiac arrhythmias, liver fibrosis)
searchTerms: iron overload causing heart and liver problems
cardiac arrhythmias and liver fibrosis due to iron
gallstones caused by chronic red cell breakdown

occasional.symptomName: Extramedullary hematopoietic masses causing spinal cord compression
searchTerms: spinal cord pressure from blood cell masses
masses outside bone marrow pressing on spine

rare.symptomName: Cardiac failure due to iron overload cardiomyopathy
searchTerms: heart muscle damage due to iron overload
cardiac problems caused by excess iron

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction including hypothyroidism and diabetes mellitus
searchTerms: hormone problems like hypothyroidism and diabetes
endocrine dysfunction with thyroid and sugar issues

rare.symptomName: Craniofacial abnormalities including frontal bossing and maxillary hypertrophy

laboratory: Microcytic hypochromic anemia with elevated reticulocyte count
Abnormal hemoglobin electrophoresis showing decreased or absent HbA and increased HbF or HbA2
Elevated serum ferritin and transferrin saturation in transfusion-dependent patients
imaging: Skull X-ray showing 'hair-on-end' appearance due to marrow expansion
MRI for iron quantification in liver and heart
genetic: Mutations or deletions in HBA1, HBA2 (alpha thalassemia) or HBB (beta thalassemia) genes

distinguishingFeatures: Low serum ferritin and iron levels
Presence of ring sideroblasts in bone marrow

redFlags: Signs of iron overload such as cardiac or liver dysfunction
Progressive bone deformities or growth retardation
references: Cappellini MD, Cohen A, Porter J, Taher A, Viprakasit V. Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion Dependent Thalassaemia (TDT). 3rd Edition. Thalassaemia International Federation; 2014.
